findings.summary: INTRODUCED BY 1d5e0d5. THE FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION OF THE REDESIGN IS FALSIFIED: 46 shapes probed against the real oracle, ~30 novel, and 8 are ADMITTED while invisible to a reader, reducing to TWO mechanisms that both need a code change. (1) <math-renderer> carries raw TeX SOURCE as its element text — `$$\hphantom{ x src/engine.ts ADR-0075 }$$` renders an invisible box but the gate reads the source and admits; same via inline $\phantom{}$, a ```math fence, a TeX `%` comment, and \color{white}. (2) GitHub's own class name says it: ```mermaid/geojson/stl/topojson fall back into <div class="render-plaintext-hidden"> inside a js-render-needs-enrichment section, replaced client-side by the diagram — a mermaid `%%` comment is not even in the diagram. Reproduced by the orchestrator end-to-end on the real driver: a body whose visible content is 'Please fix the thing. It is broken.' plus an EMPTY '## Requirements' prints PASSED — dispatchable, exit 0. ROOT CAUSE, one level down from round 3's: POST /markdown returns SANITIZED HTML, and sanitized HTML is not 'what a reader sees' — the remaining layer is CSS plus client-side hydration, and visibleTextFromHtml (:194-212) is a fresh hand-written approximation of exactly that. The rule recorded in db880fe8eaca fires on this very commit.
INTRODUCED BY 1d5e0d5: the header claims a closed class it does not have, and contradicts its own selftest.

INTRODUCED BY 1d5e0d5: `process.exit(COLLECT ? 0 : 1)` (selftest:368) tolerates ALL failures when ADM_MISS_FILE is set, not only fixture misses — observed: the same 12 genuine failures exit 1 normally and exit 0 with the variable set. A one-variable green switch inside a Brake, settable by the party being checked, and the fixture builder invokes the suite with stdio:'ignore' so it would never be seen there. Not reachable from CI. Fix: `COLLECT && failed === misses`.

the fixture cache is currently sound and its failure modes behave: 71 recorded / 71 used / 0 orphaned / 0 missing (instrumented); deleting one key is fatal offline; a fully corrupted cache fails offline; --live genuinely bypasses the cache; 98 ok offline AND 98 ok --live against the real oracle in 34.9 s
